MINUTES
  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  JANUARY 15, 2019

  1.  CALL TO ORDER

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN called the meeting to order at 7:20 p.m.

  2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Chair Zuckerman, Bacinksi, Uppal,
  Radocchio, Chan-Southwell, Larson,
  Stegura

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Retz, Schachter

  STAFF PRESENT:  Assistant to the City Manager Davis
  Sr. Planner Naughton
  Administrative Assistant Corea

  3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES, NOVEMBER
  7, 2018

  A motion was made to approve the corrected Environmental Advisory Committee Minutes
  of November 7, 2018.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

  4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  None

  5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A.  RALPH M. BROWN ACT

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that being that the Environmental Advisory
  Committee is appointed and is an advisory committee to a larger legislative body, the
  Brown Act applies. She provided a brief summary on the Brown Act and stated that there
  will be opportunity for Committee Members to participate in a training session.

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA, Assistant to the City
  Manager Davis, stated that she will inquire about the availability of web-based training.

Minutes  1
Environmental Advisory Committee Meeting, January 15, 2019
   B.  CLEAR POWER ALLIANCE DEFAULT RATE TIER SELECTION (NON-RESIDENTIAL)

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that the City has chosen 100% for the default choice for
  residential customers and information is being sent to give them the choice to opt-down
  or opt-out. Since, the City was the first to join the CPA, there is an option to choose a
  different rate for non-residential customers. CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that the EAC
  should consider, 1) non-residential customers represent a small portion of the city’s overall
  customer accounts, compared to residential; 2) some businesses in the City struggle; and
  3) a decision on the city’s default rate.

  Sr. Planner Naughton provided a PowerPoint presentation with background on the CPA
  Program and a summary of the staff report. There are 10 cities in the program who have
  defaulted to the 100% rate. Sr. Planner Naughton stated that residents should have
  received the first two notices. The service will begin in February and two additional notices
  will be sent post-enrollment with information on the program. The City will be sending a
  notice to all residents this week with brief information on the program and contact
  information.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI asked about the administrative cost of the CPA.
  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that he will provide that information.

  A discussion ensued regarding business inquiries, notifications to customers, and the
  possibility of incentivizing small businesses. Staff agreed to provide ideas on incentives
  for businesses who choose the 50% or 100% rate level.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  BACINSKI to,

  RECOMMEND TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO CHOOSE THE 36% RATE LEVEL
  FOR NON-RESIDENTIAL CUSTOMERS.

  Ayes: Chair Zuckerman, Bacinksi, Uppal, Radocchio, Chan-Southwell, Larson, Stegura
  Noes:
  Absent: Retz, Schachter
  Abstain:

  Sr. Planner Naughton suggested that the EAC decide on a default rate specific to
  Municipal Facilities.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that it is the city’s opportunity to show leadership and,
  although it is an expense, when measured against other uses, this expense is reasonable.
  COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI commented that the city should lead by example,
  since the default rate for residential is 100% green power.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN made a motion to,

  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO SET THE CITY
  FACILITIES RATE LEVEL TO 100%.

Minutes  2
Environmental Advisory Committee Meeting, January 15, 2019
   Ayes: Chair Zuckerman, Bacinksi, Uppal, Radocchio, Chan-Southwell, Larson, Stegura
  Noes:
  Absent: Retz, Schachter
  Abstain:

  C.  SUSTAINABILITY ELEMENT UPDATE

  Sr. Planner Naughton stated that the city applied for a sustainability grant through the
  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) and were given funding in the
  amount of $50K to create a stand-alone sustainability element. In working with SCAG on
  the budget, a significant cost savings was to utilize the EAC as the stakeholder committee
  for the sustainability element. It is requested that three additional EAC meetings be held
  which will be specific to the sustainability element, with the first meeting to be held in about
  April.

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA, Sr. Planner Naughton
  stated that the consultant currently working on the General Plan Update has agreed to
  collaborate with the consultant for the sustainability element. In addition, Sr. Planner
  Naughton stated that in looking for the scope she was very specific in her application, that
  this element be city specific.

  A discussion ensued on the definition of vehicle miles travelled which is used to measure
  traffic impacts.

  D.  CITY EARTH DAY CELEBRATION

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that various organizations participate in this
  event which is held at the Promenade Mall. This would be an opportunity to hear from
  community members on the sustainability element and also an opportunity to answer
  questions on the CPA Program.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER CHAN-SOUTHWELL stated that during the time she was part of
  the planning team, the different school clubs were encouraged to participate, as well as
  the various organizations, and performances and the event was very successful. Assistant
  to the City Manager Davis added that more recent years have included youth groups.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that the event is currently scheduled on
  Wednesday, April 17th. The Committee agreed to stay with this date and debrief after the
  event to determine if Saturday should be considered in the future. Committee Members
  Uppal and Bacinski stated that they would participate on the Earth Day planning team.

  E.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE 2019 GOAL SETTING

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a list of 2019 goals. The EAC’s collaboration
  with the sustainability element will be added to the list of 2019 goals. Staff made a request,
  that as committee members see articles or information relevant to the EAC, that it be
  forwarded to staff so that it could be shared with the committee members.

Minutes  3
Environmental Advisory Committee Meeting, January 15, 2019
   The city received a grant for EV charging stations and staff may be asking for guidance.
  COMMITTEE MEMBER LARSON suggested the topic of water conservation.

  Sr. Planner Naughton stated that the city will be participating in the Homeless Count on
  the Peninsula on January 23, 2019 and stated that there is a need for volunteers.

  6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS

  None

  7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  None

  8.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the meeting at 9:08 p.m.
